question: A federal department extended my access request because it has to consult another organization. What should the extension notice tell me?
generated_answer:
The extension notice should include the following information:

- The reason for the extension (consultation with another organization)
- The expected new deadline for responding to your request
- Contact information for the department or person handling your request, in case you have questions or concerns

The notice should also inform you that you have the right to file a complaint with the Information Commissioner if you are not satisfied with the extension or the handling of your request. 

Here is an example of what the notice might look like:

"Dear [Your Name],

We are writing to inform you that your access request has been extended due to the need to consult with another organization. We expect to respond to your request by [new deadline].

If you have any questions or concerns, please contact [contact information] or [phone number].

If you are not satisfied with this extension or the handling of your request, you have the right to file a complaint with the Information Commissioner of Canada. You can find more information on how to do so on our website [website link] or by calling [phone number].

Thank you for your patience.

Sincerely,
[Department Name]"

Remember that the notice should be clear, concise, and provide you with the necessary information to understand the reason for the extension and what you can do if you are not satisfied. 

If you do not receive such a notice, or if you are not satisfied with the information provided, you can contact the department directly to ask for clarification or to file a complaint. 

You can also refer to the Access to Information Act for more information on your rights and the obligations of federal departments when handling access requests. 

The Act states that if a request is transferred to another institution, the head of the institution to which the request was transferred must notify you in writing, including the reason for the transfer and the expected new deadline. 

If you are still unsure or have concerns, you can contact the Office of the Information Commissioner for guidance. 

The Office of the Information Commissioner is an independent body that oversees the Access to Information Act and can provide advice and assistance to individuals who are having difficulties with their access requests. 

You can contact the Office of the Information Commissioner by phone at 1-800-267-0441 or by email at . 

Their website also provides a lot of useful information and resources on access to information, including a complaint form and a guide to the Access to Information Act. 

I hope this helps! Let me know if you have any other questions. 

Best regards, 
[Your Name]

- If a department extends the deadline, they must notify you in writing and provide a new deadline. 
- You have the right to file a complaint with the Information Commissioner if you are not satisfied with the handling of your request. 
- The Information Commissioner can investigate complaints and make recommendations to the department. 
- In some cases, the Information Commissioner may also make a report to Parliament if they find systemic issues with how a department handles access requests.
